title: DACAPO: Accelerating Continuous Learning in Autonomous Systems for Video Analytics
problem: Continuous learning systems for video analytics in autonomous systems focus only on retraining computation while overlooking inference and labeling costs, rely on power-hungry GPUs unsuitable for battery-operated devices, and place computation on remote centralized servers causing privacy and latency issues.
motivation: Deep neural network video analytics is essential for autonomous systems like self-driving vehicles and UAVs, but real-world deployment is severely constrained by limited computational resources and battery power.
method: DACAPO combines a specialized processor with an intelligent scheduling algorithm designed to work together. The processor can divide itself into independent sections that simultaneously run inference, labeling, and retraining, with each section using only the numeric precision required for its specific task. A scheduling algorithm decides how to allocate the processor's sections and manage tasks over time, making strategic tradeoffs between accuracy and power consumption to keep the system efficient on a battery-powered device.
key_novelty: The key innovation is a processor that divides itself into sections, adapts numeric precision for different tasks, and simultaneously runs inference, labeling, and model retraining on a local device with intelligent scheduling—combining all three continuous-learning operations together rather than on remote servers or sequentially.
contributions: Hardware-algorithm co-designed accelerator for concurrent continuous learning enabling inference, labeling, and retraining on autonomous platforms
Spatially-partitionable and precision-flexible accelerator design for parallel execution of kernels at heterogeneous precisions
Spatiotemporal resource allocation algorithm for optimal resource-accuracy tradeoff navigation
Demonstrates 254× power reduction versus GPU-based systems while achieving 6.5% and 5.5% higher accuracy than Ekya and EOMU

metrics.accuracy: 6.5% higher than Ekya, 5.5% higher than EOMU
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 254× less power consumption than GPU-based systems

primary_theme: Hardware-accelerated continuous learning for autonomous systems
